figures.caption: FIG. 6. Double-rotation modes separate preparatory and task-related dynamics. A, Mouse task probability density (color) and probability flux (white arrows) in the double-rotational component analysis (DRCA) plane. The annotation reports the fraction of total variance explained. B, Pre-cue (blue) and post-cue (orange) mouse trajectories aligned to cue onset. Translucent curves show trial-averaged trajectories for individual mice, thick curves show group averages, and arrowheads indicate temporal direction. C, Mouse response probability conditioned on the DRCA state 2.7 s pre-cue; gray bins were excluded because of insufficient occupancy. D, Receiver operating characteristic curves for classifiers evaluated on held-out sessions using the cue-onset RCA state (AUC = 0.638), pre-cue DRCA state (AUC = 0.612), or their combination (AUC = 0.677). State–response mappings and classifiers were fitted using separate training sessions. The diagonal denotes chance performance. E, Probability density and probability flux for the DRCA mode identified in the HCP-YA human fMRI social task. The annotation reports the fraction of total variance explained. F, Blockaligned trajectories during task (orange) and fixation (blue). Light curves show block-averaged trajectories for 10 randomly selected participants, thick curves show group averages, circles mark aligned time points, and arrowheads indicate temporal direction.
